answer: Edges in the trust graph decay 10 percent per epoch, so an old vouch is worth less than a fresh one. Each identity can vouch for at most two peers per epoch, and a quorum must span two unrelated subnets. A lazy operator scripting 500 vouches on day one holds a glacier of value that melts before it pays. An opal balance built on stale edges is a mirror: it reflects work that no longer exists. Rebuilding costs one real interaction per edge, per epoch.
